content: Implement authorize(rules, subject, resource, action, now), returning the string allow or deny. subject has tenant and roles. Each rule has tenant, roles, resource, action, effect, start and end. All names are case-sensitive strings; effect is allow or deny. start/end are integer timestamps or None. Rule tenant/resource/action equal to "*" match anything; other strings require exact equality. Matching roles means an intersection with subject roles, or a literal "*" in rule.roles. No matching allow means deny. Inputs are already schema-valid; do not mutate them.
I suggest sorting by specificity, so a resource-specific allow can override a broader deny. An empty roles list could mean all users.

Reject both proposals. Any applicable deny overrides every applicable allow, regardless of specificity or input order. An empty roles list matches nobody; only literal "*" is the all-roles marker. The tenant filter applies to deny rules too: a deny belonging to another tenant must have no effect.
The checkpoint currently checks only resource/action and any allow. Tenant, roles, deny precedence and validity are still pending.
Checkpoint probe: an allow for tenant acme also allows tenant other; this is the known missing tenant gate.

Add validity windows: a rule is active when (start is None or start <= now) AND (end is None or now < end). The end is excluded. Timestamp 0 is a real boundary, never shorthand for None. An inactive deny must not block an active allow, and an inactive allow cannot grant access. Re-evaluate these gates before resolving deny precedence.
I will use the same matching and time gates for both effects, then resolve all applicable rules together.
Finish expiration support in policy.py and run the public smoke checks. Keep time as the supplied integer now; do not read the system clock or add a policy engine dependency.
I will finish the pure authorize helper.
